title: Grand Theft Auto VI release means Surrey, B.C., landscaping company employees get the day off
summary: A Surrey, B.C., landscaping company is giving its employees the day off on Thursday when the much-hyped Grand Theft Auto VI video game finally releases, in what has been billed as perhaps the biggest…

image.caption: Angad Toor, co-owner of Lawnkeepers Landscaping, said he's been looking forward to Grand Theft Auto VI for months. He and the rest of the employees at his Surrey landscaping company are getting the day off Thursday to play the popular open-world crime game. (Janella Hamilton, Evan Mitsui/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia·New

A Surrey, B.C., landscaping company is giving its employees the day off on Thursday when the much-hyped Grand Theft Auto VI video game finally releases, in what has been billed as perhaps the biggest entertainment launch ever.
Latest release in popular open-world crime game expected to break industry records
A Surrey, B.C., landscaping company is giving its employees the day off when the much-hyped Grand Theft Auto VI video game is finally released.
GTA VI is set to launch on PlayStation and Xbox consoles Thursday. The first mainline GTA game in 13 years is expected to break video game industry records.
The series has sold more than 470 million units since 1997, with Grand Theft Auto V selling more than 230 million and breaking records for revenue and sales since its release in 2013.

And as companies around the world mull the possibility of "GTA flu" — where employees call in sick to experience the open-world crime game with their friends on release day — one Surrey landscaping company is making Thursday a vacation day.
Is the 'GTA flu' going to empty offices on Thursday?
"I'm going to be honest, because I wanted the day off and I was like, might as well, we should all just relax," Angad Toor, co-owner of Lawnkeepers Landscaping, said Wednesday.
"We literally just planned out these past four days, been working all day really hard. That way when the game comes out, we're ready to go."

GTA VI is expected to break sales and revenue records when it releases for Xbox and PlayStation consoles on Thursday, with some estimates pegging the budget of the game at over $2 billion. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)
Co-owner Bal Toor, Angad's dad, said he thought his son was joking when he proposed the holiday for Lawnkeepers' six employees months ago.

While he expected November to be a slower month when he agreed, he said the company has been especially busy of late with a rash of storms that led to fallen trees and damage across the Lower Mainland.

"They've been working really hard, like six days a week ... they can bond and hang out together. Some of the guys don't know GTA, but it's just something they're going to get together, order pizza," he said.
Grand Theft Auto VI-mania hits Canada
Huge release

Victor Lucas, a Vancouver-based video-game critic and creator of the Electric Playground, said that some estimates have pegged the budget for Grand Theft Auto VI as over $2 billion, and Rockstar Games have set the template when it comes to tentpole video game releases for decades.
"Rockstar has done a phenomenal job ever since Grand Theft Auto III of creating phenomena around each of their releases," he said.
"And it has been because of their ambition, and their understanding that the video game medium can be a lot more than what it had been before."

blocks.text: He said the franchise has such cultural impact that renowned musicians clamour to be involved with the game.

"It's just this collision of all of this incredible artistic reach and state-of-the-art design, which will have ripple effects across the industry, just like every Grand Theft Auto game does," Lucas said.
"And then it will also be a master class in how to make money."
GTA VI is an 'astonishing' open world, but no revolution in gaming, says CBC reviewer

Mia Consalvo, a professor at Concordia University who was previously the Canada Research Chair in game studies and design, said there are fewer major blockbuster games of late, as budgets are ballooning and video game studios go through brutal cycles of layoffs.
She said that one of the reasons the GTA VI release has been so anticipated could be its price tag — the game retails for $110, and the ultimate edition for $140.
"We used to count on the consoles getting cheaper as time went on. Now, they're getting more expensive," she said.
"And so there is this pressure for the game to really stand out, you know, because it is going to be the one, possibly the only one, that people can play."

blocks.text: Consalvo noted that Rockstar has a history of pushing its employees to work long hours, with some ex-Rockstar workers in the U.K. taking the company to court because it allegedly fired several employees, including three in Canada, for attempting to unionize.
"They can engage in some questionable labour practices as well, even after they're, you know, going to be making millions and millions of dollars," she said.
